title: Where the SRAM Goes: Per-Symbol Attribution of Static Memory in FreeRTOS-C and Embassy-Rust IoT Firmware on a 64 KB RISC-V Microcontroller
abstract: arXiv:2610.21064v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Selecting a firmware stack for a memory-constrained microcontroller is usually guided by aggregate binary sizes, which report how much SRAM a build consumes but not where it goes or why. We address that gap with a per-symbol attribution method that decomposes static RAM into architectural categories - scheduler heap, network buffers and pools, task stacks, and linker-reserved regions - by bounding sized ELF symbols to the .data, .bss and .stack section ranges. The method is validated by reconciling every category sum exactly against the size-based totals for all sixteen builds. We apply it to eight cumulative firmware milestones, from a bare task scaffold to a full MQTT-over-Ethernet client, implemented twice, in FreeRTOS-C and in Embassy-Rust, on the CH32V203RBT6, a RISC-V microcontroller with 64 KB SRAM and an on-chip Ethernet MAC and PHY, with functional parity verified on hardware at every milestone. translated_title: SRAM 的去向：64 KB RISC-V 微控制器上 FreeRTOS-C 与 Embassy-Rust 物联网固件静态内存的逐符号归因分析
translated_abstract: 为内存受限的微控制器选择固件栈时，通常以聚合的二进制大小作为依据，它只能报告一次构建消耗多少 SRAM，却无法说明这些内存去了哪里、为何被消耗。我们用一种逐符号归因方法填补这一空白，该方法将静态 RAM 分解为架构性类别——调度器堆、网络缓冲区与内存池、任务栈以及链接器保留区域——通过将有确定大小的 ELF 符号限定到 .data、.bss 和 .stack 段范围来实现。该方法通过对所有十六次构建的各类别总和与基于 size 的总量进行精确对账而得到验证。我们将其应用于八个累积的固件里程碑，从裸任务脚手架到完整的基于以太网的 MQTT 客户端，分别在 FreeRTOS-C 与 Embassy-Rust 中实现两次，目标平台为 CH32V203RBT6——一款具有 64 KB SRAM 及片上以太网 MAC 和 PHY 的 RISC-V 微控制器，并在每个里程碑上通过硬件验证了功能对等性。该分解显示（原文在此处截断）……
tldr: 提出一种逐符号的静态 SRAM 归因方法，在 64 KB RISC-V 微控制器上将 FreeRTOS-C 与 Embassy-Rust 物联网固件的静态内存精确分解为调度器堆、网络缓冲池、任务栈和链接器保留区域等类别，并与总消耗量完全对账验证。
en_tdlr: A per-symbol attribution method that decomposes static SRAM into architectural categories—scheduler heap, network buffers, task stacks, and linker-reserved regions—is validated against size-based totals across sixteen builds of FreeRTOS-C and Embassy-Rust IoT firmware on a 64 KB RISC-V microcontroller.
